**Target:** 2026-11-08 (fixed). Every other date is a proposal.

> **This page carries no status.** It says what happens, who does it, what it needs, how long it takes, what it waits on, and where the result is recorded. Whether a row passed lives in the checklist it names, or in the `CLAUDE.md` To-Do entry it names. The counts of open rows are the size of the sitting still to run, read from the checklist files at generation time, not a verdict.

## How to read the weeks

Five lanes. Each row is one act that can be checked afterwards: one checklist sitting, one build step, one redeploy, one friend session, one decision.

- **Decide**: the user or the planner; each carries the date it starts to block.
- **Build**: Claude, often unattended on days the user is away.
- **Operate**: the user at a desk: redeploy, export, zip, send.
- **Verify**: the user running a checklist, sometimes with a second seat.
- **People**: friends: onboarding, the rehearsal, the evening itself.

Columns: what, who, needs, time (the user's hours, or Claude's build days, or the date a decision starts to block), waits on (row ids), done when (where the result is recorded). A *tentative* row waits on an approval or a decision.

## After the door opens

Undated by the planner's choice. Status for each lives in the To-Do; phase 5's four decisions come first.

- Phase 5's own plan (docs/design/phase5_plan.md) with four decisions open. Parts of its security and big-world tracks are already built (the NaN guard, the password reset tool, the silent-refusals closeout, the idle-creature network fix, creatures appearing when they walk into view, /loc), so the document needs a refresh when the decisions land.
- The server height model (design first, from docs/session_notes/handoff_server_height_model.md), then terrain tooling and the first zone with real hills. The capability the large world waits on.
- Trade slice 2: handing items to NPCs.
- Beast Master taming (the decided destination for the class), replacing the interim owner-derived pet levels.
- The spells still blocked: seven prestige-class spells, seven ports to zones that do not exist, Exsanguinate, Camouflage, Warder's Mend.
- The Bard song rework; sound (the friends build ships silent by decision); the UI theming pass, the one most visible to a new player.
- Public-host hardening, mandatory only if the server is ever reachable beyond Tailscale.
- The multi-zone epic, with the procedural dungeon as its first customer.

## Risks

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| **Thirteen hours of checklist sittings, all the user's** | Built is not done. If week 1 runs short, the ticks wait and the To-Do keeps saying pending. | Run the solo sittings first; the two-seat sections can bundle into one two-boxed evening and slide into week 2 without moving anything else. |
| **The bump day strands anyone on the old client** | A tester who misses the message cannot log in and may think the server is down. | Pick an evening, tell everyone a week ahead (d5), send the zip within the hour, keep the old server build to hand for one day. |
| **A client-side fix after the rehearsal** | A new zip for every friend already onboarded, days before the door opens. | Prefer server-side fixes in week 5; hold any export to one, before the rest of the group is onboarded. |
| **Two live bugs on the hosted server today** | A friend can attack a creature with spells from beyond its reaction range, and Charm may end at once; either reads as a broken game. | Step 0 closes both; nobody but the user is in the world before October 22 anyway. |
| **The trade window is the largest change ever merged in one evening** | A dupe or a loss here loses a tester permanently. | Built to its ten-point exploit ledger with the suites green on the branch (255 unit and 70 integration tests on October 5); its checklist runs before any friend trades. |
| **Days away from the desk** | None planned. If one appears, the redeploy, export and checklist lanes pause; Claude's build lane does not. | Week 5 is slack by design and absorbs a few days. A week away moves the rehearsal, not the door. |
| **Historical gaps of three to ten days** | About a week of drift per six, already seen twice. | Build steps are laid out at half the plan's pace, the schedule's own rule. |

## Assumptions

- A checklist row takes about six minutes to run, so a sitting of 15 to 20 rows is one and a half to two hours. *Source: This project's own sittings (handoff note, 2026-10-05); phase 4's 28 rows ran across five sittings.*
- A redeploy costs the user about fifteen minutes and takes the world down for about two minutes. Everyone online loses up to a minute of progress, so people log out first. *Source: docs/deployment/server_operations.md; the 2026-10-05 redeploy was down about two minutes.*
- An export plus zipping and sending it costs about an hour of the user's time. No export has been timed; this is a guess. *Source: Assumption.*
- Build steps are laid out at roughly half the pace the plan file estimates, with a review pass folded into each. That is the schedule's own rule (two-week windows for work measured at three days), because the history holds real gaps of three and ten days. *Source: docs/schedule.md section 1; docs/design/spell_batch_plan_2026_10_05.md step estimates.*
- Onboarding one friend costs the user about thirty minutes (share link, zip, README, check the account list), plus the friend's own install time. *Source: docs/deployment/inviting_a_player.md, steps 2 to 5.*
- The user has about thirty hours a week. Weeks here never schedule more than half of it, because the pile of unverified work has been the recurring risk, not a shortage of plans. *Source: docs/schedule.md header.*
- Every date here except November 8 is a proposal. The milestones were placed by working back from November 8 at the measured pace with the fifth week left as slack. *Source: The handoff's instruction; docs/schedule.md section 1.*

## Words used here

- **The R720.** The physical server in the basement that runs the game for everyone. Reachable only over Tailscale, a private network each tester joins once.
- **Redeploy.** Putting a new server build on the R720. The user's job, about fifteen minutes; the world is down about two minutes. A server change reaches players only this way.
- **Export.** Building a new game client (the program testers run) from the Godot editor, then zipping it and sending it. A client change reaches players only this way; the server needs nothing.
- **Protocol bump.** A change to the language the client and server speak. Afterwards an old client cannot connect at all, so the server and the new client must change on the same evening and every tester needs the new zip.
- **Second seat (two-boxing).** A row that needs two players in the world at once. The user can run two accounts on one machine, so no friend is required for these.
- **Checklist.** A file in docs/playtest_notes/ with one row per thing to try in the game. Filling it is how built work becomes done. The counts on this page are rows still to run; the verdicts live in the file.
- **The To-Do.** The list in CLAUDE.md. The only place an item's status lives. Nothing on this page says whether something passed.
- **GM.** The one account with developer tools (spawn a creature, grant a level, give an item). Only the user's account has it; friends never do.
- **Tentative.** Work that waits on an approval or a decision. Shown so the whole picture is visible, styled differently so it is never mistaken for a commitment.

## How this stays current

One home per fact. This page carries dates, sequence, owner and dependencies; the `CLAUDE.md` To-Do carries status; the checklists carry verdicts; `docs/schedule.md` carries the phases. The plan file `docs/schedule_detail.toml` is the only thing a person edits here.

Claude regenerates this page in every session that changes a To-Do status or a checklist (Session workflow step 4 in `CLAUDE.md`). The procedure, three lines:

1. `python tools/schedule_detail.py` from the repo root. It stops with an error if any row names a checklist or To-Do entry that no longer exists.
2. Read its report. An unscheduled checklist with open rows, or a scheduled checklist with none left, means the plan file needs a row added, moved or removed. Edit and rerun.
3. Commit the plan file with both generated files, and republish the page at its link.
